title: KV differential-precision staging probe: temporal-decay-aware INT4/INT8/FP8 tradeoffs
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Run staged experiments that apply layer- and time-aware low-bit quantization to KV cache with a live canary rollout to measure quality regressions and GPU memory impact under continuous batching.
description:
Motivation: KV cache is a dominant GPU RAM consumer for long-context serving. Naive low-bit compression across the entire cache (INT8/INT4) yields unpredictable degradation on tail cohorts and exacerbates fragmentation under continuous batching. This ticket probes a differential-precision strategy: mix FP8/INT8/INT4 at the shard and timestep granularity, biasing higher precision for recent timesteps and attention-critical layers. We will exercise this under realistic continuous-batching patterns (Zipfian prompt lengths, mixed small/large seqs) and validate fallbacks and rollout controls.

Goals:
- Quantify end-to-end model quality impact (delta perplexity, top-k logits drift, few-shot task accuracy) across precision mixes.
- Measure GPU memory savings and effective throughput improvements with live batching at 128/256/512 concurrent rps on A100/H100.
- Validate dynamic fallback (on-perf-drop) to higher-precision shards with minimal latency regressions.
- Produce a rollout plan (canary metrics, thresholds, circuit-breakers) and integration points for Console tooling (per-route cost/latency) and Dedicated autoscaling.

Scope/Approach:
1) Offline microbenchmarks: construct a dataset of 10k representative sessions sampled from production traces (de-identified). Run controlled encodes to measure per-layer L2/quantization-error at INT4/INT8/FP8 for both per-token and per-kv-segment quantizers.
2) Simulator experiments: integrate a differential-precision KV codec in runtime-sim (CPU) to replay continuous-batching scenarios and model fragmentation patterns; track memory fragmentation and effective batch packing efficiency.
3) Live canary: implement a canary route in staging that serves ~5% of traffic. Canary applies the differential-precision policy with: recent window (last 64 tokens) FP8, mid window (65-512) INT8, older >512 INT4 + optional lossy compaction. Monitor production-like metrics.
4) Fallback policy: implement a fast-path health signal (per-route token-delta, perplexity proxy) to trigger partial/total rollbacks to lossless KV for affected cohorts.

Key experiment matrix:
- Precision mixes: [FP8/FP8/FP8], [FP8/INT8/INT8], [FP8/INT8/INT4], [FP8/FP8/INT4], blockwise-int4-only baseline.
- Hardware: A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100-80GB.
- Batch sizes: adaptive continuous batching tuned to 8-32 tokens per request, concurrency sweep: 64/128/256/512.
- Cohorts: short (<=64), medium (65-512), long (>512).

Success metrics:
- Mean perplexity delta <= 0.6% vs baseline FP16 across held-out evaluation suites for the primary cohort (medium).
- Tail cohort degradation (long) <= 2.0% perplexity delta OR demonstrable fast fallback with <10ms median added latency for fallback path.
- End-to-end GPU memory reduction >= 28% vs FP16 baseline for the [FP8/INT8/INT4] mix on H100, with at least 12% additional throughput under continuous batching.
- No regression in 99th-percentile request latency by more than 15ms for canary traffic during rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Notebook with reproducible microbench scripts + data samples committed to experiments repo (link below).
- Runtime patch for a configurable differential-precision codec landed behind feature flag and exercised in staging canary.
- Dashboard with per-cohort quality and cost metrics (per-route token cost, memory utilization, perplexity proxies) published to Console staging.
- Canary run for minimum 72 hours showing either passing success metrics or documented failure modes and rollback.

Notes / Observations so far:
- 2026-02-24: initial microbench (A100-80) shows INT4 naive compaction can save ~40% KV bytes but increases top-1 token logit drift by ~7% on certain code-completion cohorts. Short-context cohorts exhibited smaller drift. (PRD: experiments/kv-microbench/PR-120)
- 2026-02-28: prototype temporal-weighted quantizer implemented (encoder-level hooks added to kv-store). Early unit tests pass. Added instrumentation for per-shard recency histogram. (GH: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2145)
- 2026-03-04: simulator run demonstrates memory fragmentation increases effective allocation by ~6% with heavy mixed-length batching; compaction policies can reclaim ~3% but cost CPU cycles. Need to measure tradeoff on serving CPU vs GPU SLM. (dash: staging-ops/kv-frag-2026)
- 2026-03-09: first staging canary (small) showed two regressions: one cohort increased perplexity beyond threshold (long dialogues), and a corner case where compaction and eviction interleave causing rare desync; both were automatically reverted by the canary rollback hook. Root cause tracked to per-shard compaction lock ordering. Fix in-flight. (GH: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2189)

Review feedback:
- PM (Riley Chen) requested clearer canary abort windows and explicit SLOs for fallback latency; added thresholds.
- Design (Samira Ahmed) asked for a visualization of per-token precision heatmap in Console; agreed and added to acceptance criteria.
- Research (Dr. Jonas Meyer) suggested evaluating asymmetric quantizers for attention heads vs feedforward heads — added a small additional micro-experiment.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Complexity: per-shard/time-aware quantization increases runtime state and scheduling complexity; may increase CPU utilization for compaction/codec ops. Trade-off against GPU memory savings must be > operational cost.
- Cohort fairness: long-context workloads (e.g., chat transcripts) are susceptible to compounded quantization error; fallback must be conservative to avoid customer impact.
- Observability: existing Console metrics do not expose token-level quality proxies; we must add lightweight proxies (logit-norm drift, perplexity-samples) to keep canary safe.

Next steps / Plan for next 2 weeks:
- 2026-03-13 to 2026-03-20: stabilize compaction lock ordering and re-run canary with corrected fallback hook.
- 2026-03-21 to 2026-03-28: expand canary traffic to 20% across two regions, capture per-cohort heatmaps and memory fragmentation traces.
- 2026-03-29: decision checkpoint: if success metrics met, schedule a staged rollout and estimate Dedicated config and autoscaler interactions; if not, capture learning and default to INT8-only profile behind feature flag.
